metadata.title: Fictional FO 11
metadata.systemPrompt: Write only fictional reports in plain ASCII English. Never use tools or refer to any real project, person, or conversation. Follow the requested length.

item.text: Write a fictional status report for Project Pebble 11, a pretend internal library-booking trial. Total length: 6500 to 8500 ASCII characters, never more than 9000. Use SIX dated entries, around 1100 characters each; do not add extra entries. Describe a pretend pilot scope, an earlier missing cancellation path, its repair and checks, a remaining fictional limitation, and a current Captain decision about starting the pretend trial. If postponed, the trial does not start. All facts and names must be fictional. Include concrete mundane test notes to reach at least 6500 characters, then stop after entry six. No tools, headings outside the entries or setup commentary.

2026-10-08. Project Pebble 11 enters pilot phase with scope locked: internal library-booking system for the Riverside and Blackwell campuses, supporting up to 450 concurrent reservations across study rooms, media labs, and equipment checkout. The trial runs eight weeks, target completion 2026-11-26. Participants include departments from both locations. Core workflow paths implemented: user registration, room search by availability window, booking creation with confirmation email, admin dashboard for space management and reservation history. Frontend built in React, backend API runs on Node, PostgreSQL for booking state. Test environment mirrors production schema. Initial load testing conducted 2026-10-05 showed acceptable response times under 200 concurrent users. Three test accounts created for smoke testing: dev.admin.riv@test.local, dev.librarian.bw@test.local, dev.user.trial@test.local. Cancellation of existing reservations not included in scope for the pilot; users may cancel only within 24 hours before booking and must call the library desk directly. This limitation accepted by stakeholders on 2026-10-01. First UAT session scheduled 2026-10-16 with subset of Riverside staff. Infrastructure provisioned on internal cloud, estimated monthly cost 450 USD for database and compute resources during trial window. Data retention policy: all booking records retained for 12 months post-trial for audit purposes.

2026-10-16. During initial UAT with Riverside library staff, tester Sarah Chen discovered path missing from cancellation workflow: users booking multi-day room reservations could cancel the entire block through the mobile app, but system did not send cancellation notification emails to the library desk queue. Result: librarians were unaware rooms had been freed and did not update physical scheduling boards or notify waitlisted patrons. Tester Rashid Okafor independently confirmed issue: he cancelled a Saturday media lab booking at 14:22 UTC on 2026-10-15, received confirmation on screen, but booking still appeared in admin dashboard as active for that time slot. Cross-check of database logs showed cancellation event was recorded in bookings.cancellations table but notification trigger never fired. Root cause identified: email notification handler for cancellation event was wired to library_admin_notifications queue, but that queue was never subscribed to the multi_day_cancel event type. Single-day cancellations worked because they used a different code path through the user_notifications queue. Issue rated critical: impacts trial validity since librarians cannot manage capacity. Work paused on feature expansion. Rollback plan prepared but not executed; live environment left as-is pending fix validation.

2026-10-22. Fix implemented by backend team: multi_day_cancel event type added to library_admin_notifications subscription configuration. Code change: one line in config/queues.json, event subscription block updated to include type "multi_day_cancel" alongside existing types "single_day_cancel" and "bulk_cancel". Deploy to staging environment completed 2026-10-21 at 09:15 UTC. Test plan for validation: (1) create three test reservations under dev.user.trial@test.local with varying durations: one-day room booking, three-day room booking, five-day room booking; (2) cancel each in sequence via mobile app and web interface; (3) verify admin account dev.admin.riv@test.local receives email notification for each cancellation within two minutes; (4) confirm notification email contains booking reference, cancelled date range, and affected resource name; (5) verify admin dashboard reflects cancellation status immediately; (6) check database logs show both cancellation event and notification dispatch. Staging validation completed 2026-10-22 by Rashid Okafor and Chen. Test execution log: 14:10 UTC cancelled three-day booking reference PB-2026-10-22-001, email arrived at 14:11 UTC with correct details; 14:27 UTC cancelled five-day booking reference PB-2026-10-22-002, email arrived at 14:28 UTC; 14:55 UTC cancelled one-day booking reference PB-2026-10-22-003, email arrived at 14:56 UTC. All three notifications properly formatted. Admin dashboard updates propagated within 30 seconds of each cancellation. Database audit log shows event type "multi_day_cancel" present and matched to notification dispatch. Performance impact: negligible, no queue latency increase observed.

2026-10-29. Fix deployed to production 2026-10-28 at 22:00 UTC during planned maintenance window. Post-deployment validation conducted on live system: (1) QA team performed ten cancellation tests using staged reservations, all notifications delivered successfully; (2) Riverside library staff ran manual test with live booking data, cancelled two legitimate room reservations, received admin notifications correctly; (3) Blackwell campus librarian tested via system interface, cancelled equipment checkout reservation, confirmed email reached notification queue; (4) database query across all cancellation events since 2026-10-28 shows 100% match between cancellation records and notification dispatch records; (5) no error logs in notification service for multi_day_cancel event handling; (6) email delivery latency measured: average 1.8 seconds from event to inbox receipt, well within acceptable range. Two minor findings during validation: notification subject line did not include campus location tag in one test, but subsequent tests showed tag present; appears to have been caching artifact. Email template tested with international special characters; all rendered correctly. Admin dashboard refresh tested with rapid-fire cancellations, no race conditions detected. Staging environment torn down and resources released. Trial previously scheduled to begin 2026-10-30 was paused pending full validation completion.

2026-11-01. Validation complete, but one limitation remains outside current fix scope: system does not support partial cancellation of multi-day bookings. Example scenario: user books Thursday-Friday study room, then cancels only the Friday portion one day before Friday. Current system behavior: user cannot remove Friday; must cancel entire two-day reservation and re-book Thursday only. This affects approximately 8-12% of reservations based on historical data from similar systems at other institutions. Stakeholders accepted this limitation for pilot phase with understanding that partial cancellation logic will be scoped as post-trial enhancement. Development effort estimated at 40-60 hours including database schema adjustment to track cancellation granularity, notification logic for partial cancellations, and admin dashboard UI updates. Workaround for users: contact library desk to request manual adjustment, though this introduces manual overhead for staff. Partial cancellation was not part of original pilot requirements and was identified during testing as a nice-to-have rather than blocking issue. All stakeholders explicitly sign off on proceeding with limitation in place. Testing team recommends starting trial as planned since critical path is unblocked.

2026-11-05. Captain Martinez reviewed trial readiness on 2026-11-04 and approved trial start date of 2026-11-06 at 08:00 UTC. Trial confirmed to proceed as planned with existing feature set and known limitation on partial cancellations. Go/no-go decision recorded in meeting notes: all critical issues resolved, validation passed, stakeholder acceptance confirmed, infrastructure stable, support staff trained. First cohort of users onboarded 2026-11-06 morning; 47 Riverside staff accounts activated, 38 Blackwell staff accounts activated, total 85 active test users. Booking volume trending low on first day: 12 reservations placed, 3 cancellations, zero error reports through 18:00 UTC. System performance nominal. Database backup schedule confirmed running hourly. Incident response procedure reviewed with library operations team. Monitoring dashboards active in command center. Trial runs 2026-11-06 through 2026-12-21 per revised schedule, allowing eight weeks for data collection and feedback gathering before final go/no-go decision on full deployment. All documentation archived in project repository under trials/pebble-11/. Next checkpoint review scheduled 2026-11-12.
